children: Mexico’s air force has ordered a second C-130J-30 Super Hercules tactical airlifter from Lockheed Martin
, expanding a fleet modernization program that began with its first order earlier this year.
The Fuerza Aérea Mexicana recently announced the acquisition, Lockheed Martin
said Tuesday. Mexico ordered its first C-130J-30 in January, becoming the first Latin American country to join the Super Hercules fleet.

another sale for a mature military transport program that has accumulated a global fleet of more than 570 aircraft. For investors, Mexico’s follow-on purchase also demonstrates continued international demand for the C-130J as governments replace aging tactical airlift fleets. Lockheed
didn’t disclose the value of the Mexican order.

Mexico has operated C-130 Hercules aircraft for more than five decades. The country is replacing older aircraft with the C-130J-30, a stretched version of the Super Hercules that provides an additional 15 feet (4.57 meters) of cargo space.
The newer aircraft also offers improvements in range, payload capacity, fuel efficiency and power compared with earlier generations, according to Lockheed
. Mexico can carry over some of its existing operational, maintenance and logistics experience as it transitions to the newer model.
Mexico’s first C-130J-30 has already been used to transport emergency supplies, medical aid and personnel following earthquakes in Venezuela, Lockheed
said. Adding a second aircraft will increase Mexico’s capacity to conduct humanitarian missions while supporting military airlift and regional security operations.

The C-130J is designed for a broad range of missions, including airdrop operations, search and rescue, firefighting, medical evacuation, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance and special operations. The aircraft is certified for 20 mission sets.
The Mexican purchase also expands the C-130J’s presence in Latin America and gives the country an aircraft that can operate alongside U.S. and allied forces.
builds the C-130J Super Hercules in Marietta, Georgia.

title: Lockheed Martin says Mexico orders second Super Hercules
